Mainly to make sure mail/absentee ballots actually arrive on time. Because the Postal Service has experienced slowdowns and most states require ballots to be *received* (not just postmarked) by Election Day, officials warned that ballots mailed in the final days might arrive too late and be rejected. Dropping a ballot in an official drop box delivers it straight into election officials' custody, bypassing the mail entirely. Officials also point out that drop boxes are free (no postage needed), available around the clock, convenient, and secure — they are locked, tamper-resistant, often under video surveillance, and emptied on a set schedule by trained or bipartisan teams with chain-of-custody logs — and using them helps voters avoid long Election Day lines at polling places.
